derivedFrom: the decision that a suspect name is asked for again on the five nights after it is marked and weekly after that, not a run. A name whose refetch fails on the night an action lands on it is marked with no retries counted; it is asked for again on each of the next five nights, each failure counting one more; after the fifth it is asked for again on the first session seven or more calendar days after the session it was last asked for, each failure counting one more, and it is named as spent on the sessions between; a night an action lands on it again asks for it and starts the count at none, and the night after asks again. The sessions are the exchange's from 2026-08-10, the session AAPL's captured action is dated, and are written here so the weeks can be read, while the test reads them off the closure table as well: the fifth retry is on Monday 2026-08-17, so the weeks come round on Monday 2026-08-24 and Monday 2026-08-31, then on Tuesday 2026-09-08 because the exchange closed on Monday 2026-09-07 for Labor Day, and then on Tuesday 2026-09-15 and not on Monday 2026-09-14, which is six days on. The action that lands on the first night and again on Wednesday 2026-09-16 is the test's own, dated on each of those two sessions. So the per-name requests the check makes for the name are one on each of the first six nights, one on each weekly night and none between, and one on each of the last two, and one action's failure costs six requests over its first six nights.
